There are, in fact, as is well-known, three major consequences of autocorrelated errors in regression analysis:

The first two points are well documented. For the remainder of this paper, we shall concentrate on the third point, and, in particular, examine the potent&alities for ‘discovering’ spurious relationships which appear to us to be inherent in a good deal of current econometric methodology.

sections.title: Simulation 1: independent random walks and inflated t-statistics

sections.summary: Argues that strongly autocorrelated residuals imply mis-specification whatever R2; reviews remedies (lagged dependent, first differences, AR(1) residuals), recommends first differencing and building levels/changes models, discusses residual-based single-series modeling, and addresses structural versus reduced-form and “good theory” in light of residual properties.
sections.title: Discussion: mis-specification, differencing, and structural debate

type.reason: Methodological econometric study with simulation evidence; it analyzes spurious regressions from autocorrelated time series and validates them with Monte Carlo experiments.
